chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayaba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah created Hawwa from Adam, so the keenness/desire of the women is [directed toward] the men; therefore, fortify/guard them in the houses.
ai.seo_question: What is the reason given in Shia hadith for women being guarded in the houses?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a metaphysical rationale for domestic modesty by linking women's psychological disposition ('himma') directly to their creation from Adam, thereby framing the home as a sanctuary for preserving marital harmony. This view is often contextualized within Shia jurisprudence not as absolute confinement, but as a protective measure against fitna (temptation), emphasizing the husband's role in 'fortifying' the wife through marriage and care.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Sayaba, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Created Hawwa<sup>as</sup> from Adam<sup>as</sup>, so the keenness of the women are the men, therefore fortify them in the houses’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn Sayabah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Allah created the creatures from Eve and Adam. The ambition of women is for men and their fortresses are the homes.’”
